title: Tolerance to long-term exposure of suspended benthic sediments and drill cuttings in the cold-water coral Lophelia pertusa
rationale: The abstract explicitly reports an experimental study on a cold-water coral (Lophelia pertusa) exposed to suspended benthic sediments and drill cuttings for 12 weeks. Measured responses include skeletal growth, polyp extension, respiration, tissue/fatty acid composition, mucus release, and larval vulnerability. This matches all CORE_INCLUDE criteria: relevant organism, explicit sediment/drill-cuttings exposure, and observed/measured biological responses. The study is substantive and directly on-topic. No other category is preferable; it is not merely a citation lead, not tropical, and not uncertain.
stressor_evidence: Suspended benthic sediments (<63 μm) and water-based drill cuttings at concentrations ~5 and ~25 mg/L
response_evidence: Reduced skeletal growth at higher particle concentrations; decreased polyp extension; no significant impact on respiration or tissue/fatty acids; low mucus release; pilot evidence of larval vulnerability
reviewer_note: Accepted without change during completed human review.
